tasks.title: Profile and Fix (Someone Else's Repo)
tasks.why: Pick an open-source project I actually use, profile a real workflow in it, and find a function taking >50ms with a flame graph. Open a PR if a small safe fix exists; either way open an issue with the flame graph, the specific function, and the numbers. Document the before/after in my journal.

tasks.title: Find an N+1 Query (Bonus)
tasks.why: Pick an open-source web app, turn on SQL logging, and browse around looking for a page issuing N+1 queries. If I find one: open an issue with the query log as evidence, and a PR if the fix is a small eager load or JOIN. If I don't find one, note it in the journal and move on.

tasks.title: Read 3 Real Flame Graphs
tasks.why: Find any 3 flame graphs published online and write in my journal, in my own words, what each one says: what's hot, and what the bottleneck is.

tasks.title: Use a Real Debugger
tasks.why: Pick a debugger for my primary language (pdb, Chrome DevTools, dlv, lldb) and solve one bug end-to-end with breakpoints. No print statements. Document the experience.

tasks.title: Soft Skill: Intellectual Humility
tasks.why: Performance work is humbling and intuition is usually wrong. Practice: state a hypothesis before measuring, say it out loud when the data proves me wrong, and keep a wrong-predictions journal to spot where my gut systematically fails.
